What if the cordless drill/driver is a little slow?
Cordless-style tool (also known as cordless drill) is a device that is battery powered. The battery is charged using standard household AC power, either by wall plug or by a high-capacity generator. The energy source is converted to power by the DC to AC inverter (also known as battery charger) and stored in rechargeable battery cells. The output power generated by the battery can be used to drive an electric motor, which is attached to a chuck or bit, creating a rotating drill. The motor is usually a lead-acid type and is connected to the chuck or bit, which in turn produces torque to operate the drill bit. For this reason, the cordless drill/driver is also referred to as a drill/driver (also known as rotary tool, or drill). Drilling is powered by the motor, while driving is powered by the impact (also known as hammer) that the tool applies to the material being chipped away by the drill bit.

The first factor is related to the motor being used in the drill/driver. A general guideline is the power, or torque, being generated by the motor. Turboshaft motors are the most widely used in cordless-style tools (such as drills). They drive the chuck of the drill/driver and generate the force to rotate the drill bits and attachments. This torque is what determines the speed of drilling and driving. There are various types of motor in the market and it can be difficult to know what type of motor is best suited for your DIY projects. The second factor involves the battery that the motor is powered by. Depending on the model, a cordless drill/driver can be equipped with a Li-ion or Ni-MH battery. There is a lot of debate on the advantages and disadvantages of these batteries when it comes to the performance and longevity of the tool. If you want a cordless tool with a lot of power, a strong battery is an important consideration for you. The third factor of performance is related to the chuck of the tool. A good chuck is the key to drilling and driving with precision.
